summary: Frontend-only verification of the new 'Сатоши' chat assistant (client-side, no backend) and lead-form regression on the preview URL. All chat flows work: launcher visible with '1' badge, click opens panel and hides launcher/badge; ~500ms typing then greeting bot message renders in #chat-messages; six quick-reply chips (price/duration/age/format/safety/signup) render with correct data-testids; clicking a chip appends a user message then a bot answer; chips with cta:true (price, signup) and the fallback both render a 'Записаться на курс' button (data-testid=chat-cta-signup); free-text 'сколько стоит?' → price answer, 'а это не мошенничество?' → safety answer, gibberish 'asdfgh' → fallback + CTA; clicking the CTA closes the panel and scrolls to #signup; chat-close hides the panel and restores the launcher. Lead-form regression: with the new hidden honeypot field 'website' present, a normal submit (lead-name-input + lead-contact-input + lead-submit) fires POST /api/leads, success-toast (data-testid=success-toast) gets .show, and GET /api/leads count grows by 1 (0 → 1). Honeypot input is properly hidden from users via .hp {position:absolute; left:-9999px; opacity:0; pointer-events:none}.
action_items: OPTIONAL: assistant.js uses substring keyword matching on normalized (lowercased, ё→е) text. This is intentionally simple and works for the reviewed queries. Consider adding a couple more synonyms per KB entry over time (e.g. 'скам' already present; add 'обманут', 'кинуть' for safety) — not blocking.

OPTIONAL: The chat-messages CTA-container bot bubble is emitted as a .chat-msg.bot with transparent background — semantically fine, but selecting the 'last bot answer' in tests requires filtering out CTA containers (e.g. `.chat-msg.bot:not(:has(button))`) to avoid false negatives.
OPTIONAL (existing): Tailwind loaded via cdn.tailwindcss.com still prints a production warning in console.
critical_code_review_comments: assistant.js is an IIFE that guards on !launcher || !panel and safely no-ops if markup is missing — good.
findAnswer() picks the KB entry with the highest keyword-hit count, tie-breaking by first-seen — deterministic and sufficient for the curated KB.
openPanel() is idempotent for greeting via the `opened` flag — greeting + chips are rendered exactly once per session; subsequent opens preserve history. Verified in browser.
CTA button click closes the panel, scrolls to #signup, and re-focuses lead-name-input after 700ms — good UX.

Honeypot markup: <div class='hp' aria-hidden='true'> with .hp {position:absolute; left:-9999px; opacity:0; pointer-events:none} — visually hidden and non-interactive but still submitted. Playwright's is_visible() returns True for off-screen positioning (misleading); confirmed via bounding-rect / computed-style that real users cannot see or interact with it.
Lead form regression clean: honeypot field addition did not affect valid submissions — POST /api/leads → 200, DB count grew 0 → 1, success toast displayed.

success_rate.frontend: 100% — all chat + lead-form regression checks passed

test_credentials: N/A — no auth in this app
seed_data_creation: One TEST_UI_<timestamp> lead was inserted via the browser Playwright run into the 'leads' MongoDB collection.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Chat assistant is fully client-side (/app/frontend/public/assistant.js) — no backend calls. Data-testids: chat-launcher, chat-panel, chat-messages, chat-chips-*, chat-form, chat-input, chat-send, chat-close, chat-cta-signup. When asserting bot answers in Playwright, note that entries with cta:true or scrollTo append an EXTRA .chat-msg.bot wrapper containing only a button — don't use `.last` for the answer text; filter to `.chat-msg.bot:not(:has(button))` or check `.all_text_contents()[-2]`. Honeypot #lf-website is positioned off-screen via .hp — is_visible() returns True but it is not user-visible; verify via bounding rect (left:-9999).
rca of the issue: No issue found. Both the chat assistant and lead-form regression work end-to-end in a real Chromium against the preview URL.
